clue.text: Original form of Covid 19 not yet found

indicators.note: the letters must be put back into some earlier, original arrangement, which signals an anagram

parts.note: a cross-reference to the solution of 19 down, ENDURES

explanation.surface: A remark that the earliest version of the coronavirus has still not been tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covid 19' reads as the disease's name, but 19 points to the answer at 19 down. 'Original form of' asks for the anagram of COVID plus ENDURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undiscovered has not been located or come to light yet.

clue.text: Eggs swell with sulphur settling to the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so the named letter sinks from the top of the word to its foot

parts.note: a swell or surge is a rising rush of water
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A kitchen picture: eggs puffing up in a sulphurous pan with the smell sinking low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in eggs on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to spur or encourage them, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Critic to ban mechanisation in farming?

definitions.meaning: a critic is someone who disparages or belittles
read as DE- (remove) plus TRACTOR: to take the tractors off the farm

explanation.surface: A detractor described as someone opposed to modern farm machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical split: the prefix de- means remove, so to de-tractor a farm is to strip its machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor is one who runs down or disparages someone, much as a critic does.

clue.text: 'Special One' recruits Doherty's left and Bale's right foot

indicators.note: to recruit is to take people into a group, so the word one takes letters inside it
a word's left side is its start, so take the first letter of the footballer's name
a word's right side is its end, so take the last letter of the footballer's name

explanation.surface: José Mourinho, 'the Special One', signing players with Doherty's left foot and Bale's right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' seems to be football; it is a metrical foot in verse. 'The Special One' is José Mourinho's nickname; Matt Doherty and Gareth Bale played for his Tottenham side.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a spondee is a metrical unit of two stressed syllables, one kind of foot.

clue.text: Meet a reporter to describe upcoming work in theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters read from bottom to top
to describe here is to draw round, so the words enclose the answer's letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to meet a journalist and tell them about a forthcoming stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' hides ETAREPO inside 'Meet a reporter', and 'upcoming' turns it upwards. 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons perform surgery in an operating theatre, so working there is doing surgery.

clue.text: Heartlessly xenophobic about a parting alien? Just so

indicators.note: the two letters for alien are parted, held apart by the other letters placed between them

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters go around the a
with its heart gone, only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A xenophobe who loathes foreigners being told off about a departing alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' reads as departing; here it means split open. 'Just so' is the definition, not a closing remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Just so means precisely or correct in every detail, which is what exact means.

clue.text: Family bathed in almost continuous lights

indicators.note: the family word is immersed in the other word, so it goes inside it
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: continuous means unending, endless
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A family soaking under almost non-stop lights, like at a spa or show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb: sets alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To enkindle is to set fire to or ignite, so it lights something.

clue.text: You might be asked to come up and see these electronic items around college

definitions.text: You might be asked to come up and see these

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: the word for items goes around the abbreviation for college

parts.note: items are things, objects

explanation.surface: An invitation to view gadgets kept at a college, like a tour of a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the old chat-up line 'come up and see my etchings', a pretext to invite someone upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The joking seduction line names engraved prints as the bait for a visit upstairs.

clue.text: Short acting lesson made shorter

indicators.note: the word is cut back at its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: a drama class is a lesson in acting

explanation.surface: A brief acting class that got cut even further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' seems to describe the lesson, but it is the noun: a short is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small drink of whisky or another spirit, which in Britain is called a short.

clue.text: He's good at balancing Telegraph puzzles with IT work

indicators.note: to puzzle the letters is to confuse or jumble them, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who juggles the Telegraph crossword alongside an IT job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzles' looks like crossword puzzles in the Telegraph newspaper, but it is the verb meaning baffles, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer on a high wire must be expert at keeping balance.

clue.text: The other half of Dutch budget

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is a wife, and a wife's other half is her spouse
to budget is to manage resources thriftily

explanation.surface: Splitting a Dutch budget, perhaps going Dutch on costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the nationality; in Cockney rhyming slang (Duchess of Fife) 'my old Dutch' means my wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife's partner is her spouse, and to husband money is to economise with it carefully.

clue.text: Not a drunken follower of Falstaff but the opposite

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: Corporal Nym is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Someone is not one of Falstaff's tipsy hangers-on, but quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' is rearranged to ANTO. Nym is a follower of Falstaff in The Merry Wives of Windsor and Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning the reverse of another, like hot for cold, is its contrary term.

clue.text: Wally's clothing for golf hotel after dark

definitions.note: a phrase for the hours of darkness, standing for the noun

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap around, so the fool's word goes around the two letters

parts.note: a wally is a fool, a nit in British slang
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fool's outfit for a golf hotel's evening do.
explanation.walkthrough: A wally is a British word for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours after dark are the period of darkness between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: New church to accommodate singers of Jerusalem, where East meets West?

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house or take in, so the singers go inside

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
the Women's Institute traditionally sings the hymn Jerusalem at meetings

explanation.surface: A new church making room for a choir singing Blake's hymn, a meeting of traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute), a British women's organisation, is famous for singing Jerusalem. The prime meridian at the London district divides eastern and western hemispheres.
explanation.definitionFit: The zero meridian of longitude runs through the observatory there, the line splitting Earth's eastern and western halves.

clue.text: For good measure, not married with new partner

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for married is taken away

parts.note: a meter is a measuring instrument
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone separated, now with a new partner for good measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For good measure' looks like a set phrase, but the definition is 'For good' and 'measure' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: For good means forever, for all time, always.

clue.text: Tree as regularly picked

indicators.note: picking letters at regular intervals means taking every other one, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tree whose leaves are harvested at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the tea plant is a tree or bush whose leaves are plucked on a regular cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia shrub grown on plantations has its leaves plucked repeatedly through the season for brewing.

clue.text: Young hare makes for dead trees?

parts.note: young means new
to hare is to run very fast, to sprint

explanation.surface: A baby hare running through a forest of fallen trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hare' seems to be the animal but is the verb, to run fast. 'Dead trees' is a jokey term for paper, made from pulped wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap paper for newspapers is made from wood pulp, so it is the remains of felled timber.

clue.text: With joyous heart, Middle-easterner is climbing Mecca

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: a Semite is a member of a people of the Middle East, such as Arabs or Jews

explanation.surface: A joyful Arab pilgrim making the ascent to Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mecca' looks like the holy city, but it is a magnet for climbers: the Californian national park with its granite walls.
explanation.definitionFit: The park's El Capitan and Half Dome make it a famous destination for rock climbers worldwide.

clue.text: Lance Armstrong at the front — he'd set about it to go first

parts.note: a lance is a spear

indicators.note: set about here means placed around, so the two-letter word surrounds the chosen letter

parts.note: the contraction written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lance Armstrong leading the cycling pack, setting about the race to take first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lance Armstrong' reads as the cyclist; it splits into a weapon and the source of A.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead a campaign is to lead it, at the head of everyone else.

clue.text: Deer getting frisky with sun bears

indicators.note: frisky letters frolic about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Deer frolicking in the sunshine alongside bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animal, in keeping with the deer, but it is the verb meaning tolerates.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with or withstand it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Polish alternative government to deliver alternative speech

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the gerund, the act of supplying it

parts.note: dubbin is a grease for softening and waterproofing leather, used instead of shoe polish

explanation.surface: An alternative government in Poland broadcasting a rival speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, with its capital, but it is the shoe polish. 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Replacing a film's soundtrack with lines in another language gives the actors substitute dialogue.

clue.text: Rugby club women as an afterthought

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A rugby club that remembers its women's side only as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasps is a well-known English rugby union club.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Premiership rugby union side is named after the stinging insects.

clue.text: Line of sunbeam reflected in Earth

indicators.note: the reversed beam is placed in the middle of the earth word

parts.note: land is earth, the ground

indicators.note: reflected light bounces back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sunbeam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A line of sunlight bouncing off the Earth's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a line of light, but it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship a lanyard is a short rope or cord, a nautical line.

clue.text: Saul of Tarsus reveals place of conversion?

indicators.note: the words reveal what is inside them, so the letters are found within the phrase

explanation.surface: The biblical Saul, whose road to Damascus was the classic conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul was converted on the road to Damascus, but the question mark points to a home improvement: turning an attic into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is often converted into a bedroom or study, the British 'conversion' of a roof space.

clue.text: It gives instruction to stop parliament ignoring children

indicators.note: to ignore is to leave out, so the letters for children are removed

parts.note: a chamber is a house of parliament

explanation.surface: A demand to stop Parliament overlooking the young.
explanation.walkthrough: Traffic lights in Britain show amber before red, telling drivers to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: On a traffic signal the yellow-orange light warns motorists to halt unless it is unsafe to do so.

clue.text: Bishop's fitting takes place before mass religious ceremony

indicators.note: before places the piece that takes place ahead of the mass letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
apt means fitting, appropriate
is in the sense exists or occurs, as in 'the meeting is today'
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A bishop's fitting service being held before Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' suggests the church service, fitting the scene, but it is the physics M.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening with water admits a person into the Christian church, a sacrament.

clue.text: Plant having branches pollarded

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has its top cut off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: limbed means having limbs, branches

explanation.surface: A tree with its branches cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning set firmly in, a variant spelling of embed.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something firmly in a surround is to fix or set it there, to embed it.

clue.text: One talking carelessly with fellow freedom fighter leads to the inevitable gallows

parts.note: a libber, as in women's libber, campaigns for liberation

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters

parts.note: a gibbet is a gallows

explanation.surface: A careless talker and a revolutionary heading for the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freedom fighter' suggests a guerrilla, but it is a liberation campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: A frivolous chatterbox who prattles flightily is a flighty gossip.

clue.text: Squat maybe located, it's said, without planning

parts.note: squat is one kind of short, short and stocky

indicators.note: it's said marks a word spoken aloud, so its sound is what goes in

parts.note: sited means located

explanation.surface: A squat being set up without any planning permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squat' looks like a squatted building, but it is the adjective meaning stocky.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sighted policy lacks foresight, failing to look ahead to consequences.
